name: Research report generator from live web search

nodes.name: Research request form
nodes.notes:
User submits their research request here.

Form collects:
- The specific topic to research
- Who the report is for (audience)
- What the report should achieve (goal)
- Optional focus or subtopics

The workflow immediately starts two web searches
and returns a full report within 2 minutes.

parameters.formDescription: Submit a research topic and receive a complete professional research report within 2 minutes — sources gathered, analyzed, and written automatically.

nodes.name: Set config
nodes.notes:
REPLACE THESE 4 VALUES:

1. serperApiKey
   Go to serper.dev → create free account → copy API key
   Free tier: 2500 searches per month
   This workflow uses 2 searches per report

2. recipientEmail
   Who receives the research report email
   Example: you@example.com

3. senderName
   Your name for email sign-offs
   Example: Rahul Dutt

4. sheetId
   Open your Google Sheet in browser
   URL: docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1ABC123/edit
   Copy the part between /d/ and /edit
   Create a tab called: Research Log
   Row 1 headers:
   Date | Topic | Audience | Goal | Key Findings | Sources Used | Report Title | Confidence Level | Requested By | Logged At

All form fields are mapped automatically.
The expert query is auto-generated by adding context words to the main topic.
Do not change the expression fields.

nodes.name: Search the main topic
nodes.notes:
Searches Google for the main research topic using Serper API.

Returns top 10 organic results with:
- Title
- URL (link)
- Snippet (2-3 sentence summary)
- Date when available

Serper API endpoint: POST https://google.serper.dev/search
Authentication: X-API-KEY header

No changes needed.

nodes.name: Search the expert angle
nodes.notes:
Second Serper search using the expert angle query.

The expert query is auto-generated in Set Config Values:
Main Topic + expert insights data research 2026

This second search returns different results —
more likely to include research papers, expert articles,
statistics, and recent data.

Using two searches doubles the source coverage
and gives the AI much richer research material.
No changes needed.

nodes.name: Combine the sources
nodes.notes:
Merges results from both Serper searches into one research package.

Process:
- Takes top 8 results from main topic search
- Takes top 7 results from expert angle search
- Deduplicates by URL (removes any overlapping results)
- Numbers them sequentially
- Formats into a structured text block for AI analysis

Typical output: 12-15 unique sources

The researchContent field is structured so AI can
reference [Source N] when citing specific points.

No changes needed.

nodes.name: Analyse the sources
nodes.notes:
First AI agent — extracts structured intelligence from the raw research.

This is the ANALYSIS phase — not writing yet.
The agent identifies:
1. Key findings from across all sources
2. Specific data points and statistics
3. Expert positions and opinions
4. Source credibility assessment
5. Knowledge gaps not covered
6. Contradictions between sources
7. Overall research confidence score

Separating analysis from writing (two-agent approach)
gives much better report quality than a single call.

Output is in $json.output

parameters.text:
=You are a senior research analyst specializing in evidence-based intelligence gathering.

Research topic: {{ $json.mainTopic }}
Target audience: {{ $json.targetAudience }}
Research goal: {{ $json.reportGoal }}
Specific angle requested: {{ $json.specificAngle }}
Sources available: {{ $json.sourceCount }}

Research materials gathered from live web search:
{{ $json.researchContent }}

Analyze these sources and extract structured intelligence. Return ONLY a valid JSON object. No extra text. No markdown. No backticks.

Required fields:

keyFindings
Array of 5 to 8 strings. The most important facts, trends, or conclusions found across the sources. Each finding should reference specific evidence. Each under 35 words.

dataPoints
Array of 3 to 6 strings. Specific statistics, numbers, percentages, or measurable data found in the sources. If none found write: No specific data points identified in available sources.

expertPositions
Array of 2 to 5 strings. Notable expert opinions, positions, or quotes found. Each should attribute to a person or organization when identifiable.

sourceCredibility
Array of strings. Notes on which sources are most authoritative or recent. Mention 3 to 5 specific sources by number.

knowledgeGaps
Array of 2 to 4 strings. Important questions about this topic that the research did NOT clearly answer. These are blind spots worth flagging.

contradictions
Array of strings. Any conflicting information or disagreements between sources. Empty array if no contradictions found.

researchConfidence
Number from 1 to 10. How well do the sources cover the research topic?
1 to 3: poor coverage, many gaps.
4 to 6: moderate coverage with some gaps.
7 to 8: good coverage of the main points.
9 to 10: excellent coverage with strong evidence.

nodes.notes:
Schema: 7 required fields for research analysis.
Ensures Agent 1 always returns clean structured data.
No changes needed.

nodes.name: Write the report
nodes.notes:
Second AI agent — writes the professional research report.

This agent receives STRUCTURED intelligence from Agent 1
(not raw snippets) so it can focus entirely on writing quality.

The report has 8 sections:
1. Title
2. Executive summary (3-4 sentences)
3. Background context
4. Key insights (5 specific points)
5. Detailed findings (3-4 paragraphs)
6. Implications for the target audience
7. Recommended actions (4 steps)
8. Conclusion

Two-agent approach = better results:
Agent 1 handles factual accuracy.
Agent 2 handles writing quality.

Output is in $json.output

nodes.name: Chat model - Writing
nodes.notes:
Connect the same OpenAI credential here.
temperature: 0.5 for clear professional writing
Cost: about $0.004 per report

nodes.name: Output Parser - Report
nodes.notes:
Schema: 8 required fields for the research report.
Ensures Agent 2 always returns all report sections.
No changes needed.

nodes.name: Build the report email
nodes.notes:
Combines both AI agent outputs into the final deliverables.

Builds a full email with 8 sections:
1. Report title and metadata
2. Executive summary
3. Background context
4. Key insights (numbered)
5. Detailed findings
6. Implications for the audience
7. Recommended actions (numbered)
8. Knowledge gaps + all source URLs

Also prepares clean fields for the Google Sheets log row.

References:
- $json.output for the report (Agent 2)
- $('Analyse the sources').item.json.output for analysis data
- $('Combine the sources').item.json for config

No changes needed.

parameters.jsCode:
const report = $input.first().json.output;
const analysis = $('Analyse the sources').item.json.output;
const research = $('Combine the sources').item.json;

if (!report || !analysis) {
  throw new Error('AI report generation failed. Check your OpenAI credentials.');
}

const confidence = analysis.researchConfidence || 0;
const confidenceLabel = confidence >= 8 ? 'High' : confidence >= 5 ? 'Medium' : 'Low';

const keyInsights = (report.keyInsights || []).map((ins, i) => (i + 1) + '. ' + ins).join('\n');
const actions = (report.recommendedActions || []).map((a, i) => (i + 1) + '. ' + a).join('\n');
const keyFindings = (analysis.keyFindings || []).slice(0, 5).join(' | ');
const loggedAt = new Date().toISOString().replace('T', ' ').substring(0, 16);

// Build the full email body
const emailBody =
  'Hello ' + research.senderName + ',\n\n' +
  'Your research report is ready.\n\n' +
  'Topic: ' + research.mainTopic + '\n' +
  'Audience: ' + research.targetAudience + '\n' +
  'Goal: ' + research.reportGoal + '\n' +
  'Sources analyzed: ' + research.sourceCount + ' | Research confidence: ' + confidence + ' out of 10 — ' + confidenceLabel + '\n' +
  'Date: ' + research.today + '\n\n' +

  '============================================================\n' +
  report.reportTitle.toUpperCase() + '\n' +
  '============================================================\n\n' +

  'EXECUTIVE SUMMARY\n\n' +
  report.executiveSummary + '\n\n' +

  '============================================================\n' +
  'BACKGROUND\n' +
  '============================================================\n\n' +
  report.background + '\n\n' +

  '============================================================\n' +
  'KEY INSIGHTS\n' +
  '============================================================\n\n' +
  keyInsights + '\n\n' +

  '============================================================\n' +
  'DETAILED FINDINGS\n' +
  '============================================================\n\n' +
  report.detailedFindings + '\n\n' +

  '============================================================\n' +
  'IMPLICATIONS FOR ' + research.targetAudience.toUpperCase() + '\n' +
  '============================================================\n\n' +
  report.implications + '\n\n' +

  '============================================================\n' +
  'RECOMMENDED ACTIONS\n' +
  '============================================================\n\n' +
  actions + '\n\n' +

  '============================================================\n' +
  'CONCLUSION\n' +
  '============================================================\n\n' +
  report.conclusion + '\n\n' +

  '============================================================\n' +
  'KNOWLEDGE GAPS — QUESTIONS NOT FULLY ANSWERED\n' +
  '============================================================\n\n' +
  (analysis.knowledgeGaps || []).map((g, i) => (i + 1) + '. ' + g).join('\n') + '\n\n' +

  '============================================================\n' +
  'SOURCES REFERENCED (' + research.sourceCount + ' total)\n' +
  '============================================================\n\n' +
  research.sourceList + '\n\n' +

  'All research requests are logged in your Google Sheets Research Log tab.\n\n' +
  'Best regards,\n' + research.senderName;

return [{
  json: {
    emailSubject: 'Research Report: ' + report.reportTitle + ' — ' + research.today,
    emailBody,
    // Sheets fields
    today: research.today,
    mainTopic: research.mainTopic,
    targetAudience: research.targetAudience,
    reportGoal: research.reportGoal,
    keyFindings,
    sourceCount: research.sourceCount,
    reportTitle: report.reportTitle,
    confidenceLevel: confidence + ' out of 10 — ' + confidenceLabel,
    requestedBy: research.requestedBy,
    loggedAt,
    sheetId: research.sheetId,
    sheetName: research.sheetName,
    recipientEmail: research.recipientEmail
  }
}];

nodes.name: Log the request
nodes.notes:
Logs every research request to Google Sheets.

How to connect:
1. Go to console.cloud.google.com and enable Google Sheets API
2. In n8n: Settings → Credentials → Add New → Google Sheets OAuth2
3. Authenticate and connect to this node

Sheet tab: Research Log
Row 1 headers:
Date | Topic | Audience | Goal | Key Findings | Sources Used | Report Title | Confidence Level | Requested By | Logged At

Use this sheet to:

nodes.name: Email the report
nodes.notes:
Sends the complete research report to the configured email.

3. Authenticate and connect to this node

The email includes:
- Full 8-section professional report
- Knowledge gaps and open questions
- All source URLs for further reading

Typically arrives within 90 seconds of form submission.

parameters.content:
## 1. Take the request
A form asks for the topic, audience and goal of the report. One config node holds your search API key, email and sheet.

## 2. Search the web twice
One search covers the topic itself, a second looks for expert and data angles. Duplicates are dropped and up to fifteen numbered sources are combined.

## 3. Analyse, then write
The first agent pulls out findings, data points and disagreements with source numbers. The second writes the finished report for your audience and goal.

## 4. Log and deliver
The report is formatted as an email with its sources listed, logged to your sheet first, then sent.

# Research report generator from live web search

Fill in a short form with a topic, who the report is for and what it needs to achieve, and a sourced research report lands in your inbox a couple of minutes later. The workflow finds its own sources through two separate web searches, so the report is built on current information rather than whatever the model remembers.

### How it works
1. A form collects the topic, the target audience and the goal of the report.
2. One web search covers the topic directly, and a second looks for expert opinion, data and statistics on it.
3. Results from both are merged, duplicate links are dropped, and up to fifteen sources are numbered. If one search fails, the report is still written from the other.
4. The first agent analyses those sources and returns key findings, supporting data, points of disagreement and a confidence level, each tied back to a source number.
5. The second agent writes the finished report for your stated audience and goal.
6. The report is formatted into an email with its sources listed, logged to your sheet, then sent to you.

### Setup
1. Add your OpenAI API key and connect your Google Sheets and Gmail accounts.
2. Create a free Serper account for Google search results and copy your API key.
3. Open Set config and fill in the Serper key, your email, your name and your sheet ID.
4. Create a tab called Research Log with headers for Date, Topic, Audience, Goal, Key Findings, Sources Used, Report Title, Confidence Level and Requested By.
5. Activate and share the form URL.

### Customization
Change the second search query to look for case studies or competitor coverage instead of expert views.
